chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Hariz, who said:

Ismail ibn Abi Abdillah had gold coins, and a man from Quraysh wanted to travel to Yemen. Ismail said: 'O father, so-and-so wants to go to Yemen, and I have such-and-such gold coins; do you think I should give them to him to buy me goods from Yemen?' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O my son, has it not reached you that he drinks wine?' Ismail said: 'That is what the people say.' He said: 'O my son, do not do that.' But Ismail disobeyed his father and gave him his gold coins, so he lost them all and did not bring him back anything of them.

He said: 'O my son, verily Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says in His Book: “He believes in Allah and believes the believers” — meaning: he confirms the truth of Allah and considers the believers truthful. So if the believers witness something to you, then accept it from them.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on trusting the testimony of believers in financial transactions?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the Shia jurisprudential principle of 'tashih al-mu'min' (validating the testimony of a believer), where the default assumption is that a Muslim is truthful and trustworthy in financial dealings. Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies that while Quran 9:61 establishes the general reliability of believers, this presumption can be overridden by specific, known defects in character, such as the merchant's consumption of wine, which Ismail ignored to his detriment. The narrative thus balances the general rule of trust with the practical necessity of verifying individual integrity, a key concept in Shia fiqh regarding contracts and testimony.

en.ammaar-muslim: 2. [2/84] al-Kafi: Ali from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from Hariz who said:

Ismail the son of Abi Abdillah had gold coins and a man from the Quraysh wanted to set out to Yaman, so Ismail said: O father – so and so wants to set out to Yaman and I have some gold coins do you think I should give them to him to buy me some goods from Yaman? Abu Abdillah عليه السلام said: O my son – has it not reached you that he drinks wine? Ismail said: this is what the people say, he said: O my son – do not do that, but Ismail did not obey his father and gave the gold coins to him so he (that man) lost it all and did not give anything of them (back) to him…

he said: O my son – verily Allāh Mighty and Majestic says in his book: “(he) believes in Allāh and believes the believers” [9:61] – meaning: confirms the truth of Allāh and considers the believers truthful, so if the believers witness something to you then accept it from them…
